correctness.rationale: The Bessel product kernel and derivative factorization follow from the heat equation. A Riccati first-zero argument proves strict increase of each spatial logarithmic score. A spectral Laplace-transform split into disjoint intervals about 2d proves exactly one nearest-neighbor derivative sign change. The score ordering identifies all signs until this crossing; mass conservation and translation invariance give the exact endpoint norm and strict breakdown afterward. The dimension comparison and asymptotic Bessel series are explicit. Finite numeric tests do not replace these infinite arguments.

value.rationale: The boundary is motivated intrinsically as the exact first instant when the Markov heat derivative acquires negative mass away from its start. It gives a maximal sharp L1 and L∞ norm interval, an all-dimensional uniqueness and monotonicity theorem, and a controlled dimension-scaling law. It is not merely a single numeric root or the known one-dimensional Bessel identity, and the point at which the simple norm formula ceases to hold matters for endpoint semigroup smoothing bounds.
